A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DistillKac research. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching, including relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original CIFAR-10 and CelebA-64 generation results, FID comparisons, sampling timings, and hyperparameter and distillation analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original generation experiments and adds LSUN Bedroom-256 samples and quantitative teacher–student trajectory analyses in Appendix B.6.

M1.justification: Velocity-space guidance, Algorithm 1's endpoint-matching loss and frozen teacher, and the multistage distillation procedure remain unchanged. The LSUN experiments use the existing method with another UNet configuration.

E1.justification: v1 covers CIFAR-10 at 32×32 and CelebA-64 at 64×64. v2 adds training and unconditional generation on LSUN Bedroom-256, substantially extending coverage to higher-resolution indoor scenes. Figures 4–5 provide qualitative teacher and student results, although no LSUN quantitative benchmark comparison is reported.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains the same comparator methods. The updated Duong citation refers to the same Kac Flow work. Latent Consistency Models and Latent Adversarial Diffusion Distillation are newly discussed but are not added to the experimental comparisons.

E3.justification: v2 adds LSUN settings and a shared-initial-noise trajectory-comparison protocol, including comparisons over 100 samples. Table B-2 changes one reported sweep setting from (25, 5) to (100, 5). Table B-1 changes the schedule label from Warmup–Flat–Cosine to Flat–Cosine but retains 2% warmup, leaving actual warmup removal unclear. The existing 50k-sample FID protocol is retained.

E4.justification: New Appendix B.6 directly investigates the central endpoint-to-trajectory stability premise: it measures mismatch over time for 20-, 4-, 2-, and 1-step students and relates trajectory discrepancy to endpoint discrepancy. This substantially extends the earlier hyperparameter, integrator, and distillation-schedule analyses, which are retained.

E5.justification: Figure B-3 newly reports Pearson correlations and fitted linear-regression R² values across 100 sampled trajectories. This adds statistical estimation, but does not introduce repeated-training-run information, FID confidence intervals, or seed-variation reporting.

E6.justification: v2 adds LSUN generation results and direct trajectory-error findings, including correlations of 0.9992 and 0.9976 in Figure B-3. Table 2 revises CelebA-64 DistillKac FID from 6.91 to 5.66 at 2 NFE and from 9.20 to 7.45 at 1 NFE; the CIFAR-10 Kac Flow baseline changes from 6.80 to 6.42 at 100 NFE. The causes of these score revisions are not explained.

T1.justification: The formal assumptions, theorems, corollary, derivations, and Appendix A proofs are unchanged. The added introduction sentence describing diffusion as a limiting case supplies conceptual context without a new formal limit statement or derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions, and concluding position retain the same claims about finite-speed Kac flows, velocity guidance, endpoint distillation, stability, and few-step generation. The explicit absence of a state-of-the-art claim also remains.

C2.justification: Appendix B.6 adds the interpretation that endpoint mismatch almost completely explains observed trajectory discrepancy. Section 6 newly argues potential applicability to latent Kac flows and transformer architectures, without evaluating them. The introduction adds the diffusion-limit connection; the existing dimensionality and performance limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix B.1 adds LSUN hyperparameters, AMP-use flags, monitoring frequencies, training hardware, and convergence and training-time information. Hardware and monitoring details for CIFAR-10 and CelebA-64 are newly disclosed rather than established procedural changes. Code-access information is unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 6 adds a focused discussion of latent diffusion distillation, including new references to Luo et al. (2023) and Sauer et al. (2024), and positions DistillKac relative to these approaches. The Duong preprint-version/year update concerns an already cited work.

P1.justification: Changes comprise localized introductory and related-work additions, expanded experimental documentation, a new Appendix B.6 subsection, and conference headers. The main narrative and section order remain largely intact; the existing generated-image subsection moves from B.6 to B.7.

P2.justification: Visual evidence expands substantially through LSUN sample grids in Figures 4–5 and trajectory diagnostics in Figures B-2–B-3. Table B-1 gains an LSUN column and AMP row, while Table 2 is enlarged and gains group separators. Existing appendix galleries are retained as Figures B-4–B-7.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens empirical support with trajectory diagnostics and higher-resolution generation examples, while improving training-resource documentation and related-work context. These gains are limited by qualitative-only LSUN evaluation and unexplained FID revisions. Despite the new warmup-label ambiguity, the added evidence and reproducibility information support a modest net improvement.
